public_exhibition_handoff.claim_ceiling: For every simply connected planar domain of finite area, the Euclidean length of the hyperbolic geodesic between $a$ and $b$ is at most $\sqrt{(\operatorname{Area}/\pi)\log(1/(1-\rho(a,b)^2))}$, and this bound is sharp. The formula is an apparently unrecorded exact Bergman-space consequence of standard kernel covariance and area identities. Its Green/Blaschke specialization gives new sufficient criteria for selected polynomial lemniscates, but Erdős #1041 remains open.
